column1: # review-level-rules.tsv -- the path classes and floor rules /work-on's review
# level is checked against. review-levels.md says what the levels mean;
# A run reads the copy of this file `review-level.sh init` stored when its
# level was first chosen, never the working tree's, so a change here applies to
# runs that start after it lands. This file is in the `security` class below,
# so a diff that edits it floors at `full`.
# Tab-separated. Blank lines and lines starting with `#` are ignored.
#   class <name> <glob>   a path is in <name> when it matches <glob>. A class
#                         may have many globs. Globs are bash `case` patterns
#                         matched on the repository-relative path; `*` also
#                         matches `/`, and a leading `**/` also matches no
#   rule <level> <fact>   the floor is at least <level> when <fact> holds.
#                         <level> is light, standard or full. <fact> is one of
#                           class:<name>       a changed path is in the class
#                           tests_changed      a path in the `test` class changed
#                           unclassified       a changed path is in no class
# The floor is the highest level any rule yields, `light` when none fires.
# A path can be in several classes and every one counts, so `docs` (which no
# rule names) only keeps a path out of `unclassified`: README.md alone stays
# `light`, SKILL.md is `instruction` as well and floors at `standard`, and an
# unclassified source file floors at `standard`. `light` is reachable only
# when every changed path is documentation or in a class with no rule.
# review-level.sh refuses (exit 64) a file with an unknown record type, level
# or fact, or a rule naming a class no `class` line defines.
# koto templates hold the gates and the routing.
# The scripts the templates run as gates or default_actions, and the scripts
# that open sessions on them. review-level_test.sh fails when a template's
# gate or default_action command names a script no `engine` line covers.
# Text an agent follows as instructions.
# Documentation: no rule names it, so a path here and in no other class
# leaves the floor at `light`. requirements*.txt matches `*.txt` too, and the
# `manifest` class above still floors it at `standard`.
